Setting up for biomechanical analysis

Nirav Maniar

Source: vignettes/setting-up.Rmd
setting-up.Rmd

Installing 

#install the remotes package if you don't akready have it
install.packages("remotes")

#install the package
remotes::install_github("Kneerav/biomechanics")

Basic setup

To get going with the basic setup, you can just load your library.

library(biomechanics)
#> Warning: replacing previous import 'ggplot2::last_plot' by 'plotly::last_plot'
#> when loading 'biomechanics'

Please note that for full functionality, we also want the OpenSim api set up.

OpenSim api

Some functions depend on the OpenSim api (https://simtk.org/projects/opensim). To set this up, we first need to set up a Python environment.

Download and install either Anaconda or Miniconda from: https://www.anaconda.com/download. I prefer Miniconda, as it is a “lighter” version that takes up far less disk space than the full Anaoconda version (but also does not include common packages).

Next, we want to create a new environment for the OpenSim conda package to be installed. We try to use informative names, so in this instance it will be called “opensim_scripting_452_311” with python version 3.11, indicating OpenSim v4.5.2 and python version 3.11.

One way to achieve this is to open anaconda prompt and type the following:

conda create -n "opensim_scripting_452_311" python=3.11

Alternatively, you can create the same environment by opening anaconda navigator and create a new environment called “opensim_scripting_452_311” with python version 3.11.

Once the environment is created, enter the code (in the conda prompt) below to activate your new environment, install the opensim package. To install a specific version (v4.5.2 is working well at the time of writing this), we’d use the following:

conda activate opensim_scripting_452_311
conda install opensim-org::opensim==4.5.2

To install the latest version (which should be indicated here: https://anaconda.org/opensim-org/opensim), do the following instead:

conda activate opensim_scripting_452_311
conda install opensim-org::opensim

Then switch to the python interpreter to test your installation.

python
import opensim as osim

If you have no errors, you are ready to roll. If you have errors, a common issue solution I have observed is we sometimes need to downgrade the OpenSSL package to 1.1.1w (which is most easily achieved in the anaconda navigator).

Assuming the install works, you might as well install the additional python packages we might need as follows.

exit() #to leave the python interpretor
conda install -c conda-forge btk #btk has numerous tools for working with c3d files
conda install scipy=1.16 #for signal processing 
pip install spm1d #statistical parametric mapping

Note that a specific version of scipy was specified to align with OpenSim 4.5.2, since later versions are not compatible with the specific version of numpy needed for the specific version of the opensim package to work. By installing a specified version of scipy, we stop this and the spm1d install process from automatically upgrading numpy to an incompatible version. If you install another version of OpenSim, you’ll have to be careful when installing other packages in the same environment, particularly with numpy is a dependency.

Assuming that all went well, next open R Studio and ensure that the reticulate package is setup to work with our new environment. The easiest way I have found to do this is as follows:

library(reticulate) #you should have installed this package already
Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = "C:/Users/User/.conda/envs/opensim_scripting_452_311") #change file path as needed
py_discover_config() #check to see if reading correct version of python, should be 3.11
osim = import("opensim")

If no errors, you are good to go. Note that the above chunk of code needs to be run every time you use any function requiring the OpenSim-python api in a new R session (except py_discover_congif()).

Other r packages

There are plenty of other R packages worth installing. Here is a few basics:


install.packages(
  c("tidyverse", #you probably know why
    "readxl" #read excel files
    "pracma", #maths stuff
    "signal", #for signal processing
    "caroline", #some useful utility functions
    "fda", #functional data analysis
    )
  )

Note that pracma and signal are already dependencies for the biomechanics package.

Other recommended installs

I’d also recommend the following installs to make life easier:

  • OpenSim GUI - Graphical user interface for OpenSim (musculoskeletal modelling software) https://simtk.org/projects/opensim
  • Notepad ++ - text editor which is very useful for opening .xml and other files https://notepad-plus-plus.org/
  • Mokka - Motion capture data visualiser https://biomechanical-toolkit.github.io/mokka/
